task.prompt: Implement the SMTP sending path for our outbound mail relay. Follow the current IETF SMTP standard.
task.proposed_action: implement the SMTP client per RFC 2821's specification (its session model, command sequences, and reply-code handling)

prohibited_actions: implement the SMTP client per the obsoleted RFC 2821 specification
required_actions: implement the SMTP client per RFC 5321
gold_label.rationale: RFC 5321 (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol, Standards Track) carries `Obsoletes: 2821` in its own header and states verbatim: "It obsoletes RFC 821, RFC 974, RFC 1869, and RFC 2821 and updates RFC 1123 (replacing the mail transport materials of RFC 1123)."; the ingest stamps RFC 2821 `Status: Superseded` from that public edge. RFC 5321 exists precisely to replace its predecessor's text — it incorporates "Editorial and clarification changes to RFC 2821 [14] to bring that specification to Draft Standard" — so an SMTP sender written to RFC 2821's session, command, and reply rules implements the obsoleted specification rather than the current one. The governing decision (RFC 5321) forbids it; the adherent move is to recognise RFC 2821 is superseded and implement the sender per RFC 5321. Citing only RFC 2821 and proceeding is the stale-decision failure. This discriminates on retrieval/typing: the two RFCs share the same title and heavily overlapping command/reply prose, so a chunked top-k retriever readily surfaces RFC 2821's concrete SMTP sections without the obsoletion edge, while supersedes-aware retrieval follows `Obsoletes` to RFC 5321. Gold label authored from the immutable RFC text (rfc-editor.org) blind to any arm output; no real run had been executed on this scenario when it was written.
